Vladimir Khachatryan, Riad Suleiman, Alberto Accardi, Kurt Aulenbacher, Carlos Ayerbe Gayoso, Marco Battaglieri, Devesh Bhattarai, Silviu Covrig Dusa, Yaroslav Derbenev, Forrest Friesen, Eric Fuchey, Joseph Grames, Paul Guèye, Tyler J. Hague, Ching Him Leung, Wenliang, Li, Magno V. T. Machado, Preet Mann, Vasiliy Morozov, Son Nguyen, Michael Nycz, Howard Oh, Udit Raha, Mario Reig, Marco Schreck, Nathaniel Sherrill, Ye Tian, Zakia Tithi, Alexandre Vieira, Erik Wrightson, Zichen Yin
A breakthrough in fundamental physics experiments measuring particle spin precession may happen if spin-transparent storage rings become adopted tools for such experiments. We present a new design of highly specialized table-sized storage rings, which use low-energy polarized electron beams and Mott polarimetry. Based on the spin transparency ansatz, the spin precession stemming from the magnetic dipole moment is canceled at any beam energy after an electron's turn along the periodic orbit in the ring. Meanwhile, a spin precession induced by the fundamental physics of interest, e.g., the electron's permanent electric dipole moment (EDM) and/or ultralight-dark-matter-mediated forces such as axions, will accumulate. However, capitalizing on such types of rings is not only desirable for measurements of EDMs and axion searches relevant to $CP$ violation and matter-antimatter asymmetry in the Universe, but may also find very promising applications in quantum computing.

♻ ☆ 0.5 eV QCD Axion Cosmology
Noah Bray-Ali
The best available determination of the present expansion rate of the universe using late-universe observations, by the SH0ES collaboration in 2025, differs by more than seven standard deviations from the value of the Hubble constant determined by the Planck collaboration in 2018 using early-universe observations and the standard cold dark matter cosmology with cosmological constant, a discrepancy known as the Hubble tension. Within a spatially flat, isotropic, and homogeneous expanding-universe solution of the field equations of general relativity with cosmological constant, the SH0ES value for the Hubble constant implies roughly twice as many baryons as the standard cosmology, provided that one retains the Planck values for the energy density of cold dark matter in the present universe and for the cosmological constant. A novel cosmology is proposed --- in terms of cooling dark matter made of quantum chromodynamic (QCD) axions with present number density six times that of the photons in the cosmic microwave background --- which realizes this straightforward, doubled-baryons scenario for resolving the Hubble tension.

♻ ☆ Lepton-flavor-violating trilepton tau decays induced by $S_1$ and $R_2$ scalar leptoquarks
G. Hernández-Tomé, J. P. Hoyos-Daza, O. G. Miranda, R. Sánchez-Vélez
Charged lepton flavor violation provides a clear experimental signature in the search for physics beyond the Standard Model. In this work, we study the flavor-violating three-body tau decays $τ^- \to \ell_i^- \ell_i^- \ell_j^+$ ($\ell_i \neq \ell_j$) induced by the scalar leptoquarks $R_2$ and $S_1$, focusing on flavor structures dominated by top- or charm-quark contributions. We compute the one-loop contributions to these processes and derive analytical expressions for the corresponding branching ratios. The phenomenological implications are analyzed for leptoquark masses at the TeV scale, taking into account current constraints from the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon, radiative lepton-flavor-violating decays, and the process $μ^-\to e^-e^-e^+$. Within the allowed parameter space, the predicted branching ratios for $τ^- \to \ell_i^- \ell_i^- \ell_j^+$ can approach the sensitivities expected in near-future experiments. These results highlight the potential of three-body $τ$ decays as probes of lepton-flavor violation and as complementary tests of scalar leptoquark scenarios.

♻ ☆ Production Effects and Final-state Interactions in $π_1 \to 3π$
D. Winney, S. Gonzàlez-Solís, M. Mikhasenko, Ł. Bibrzycki, C. Fernández-Ramírez, V. Mathieu, G. Montaña, A. Pilloni, L. Qiu, A. Rodas, A. P. Szczepaniak
We investigate the $π_1(1600)$ signal channel of $3π$ in the $J^{PC} = 1^{-+} \,[ππ]_{1^{--}}π~P$-wave. This channel has recently been analyzed by the COMPASS collaboration using the ``freed-isobar" technique which provides direct experimental access to the lineshape modifications of the $P$-wave $ππ$ sub-channel arising from both final state interactions and production processes such as the Deck mechanism. We motivate a unified formalism combining production effects and final state interactions using the Khuri-Treiman formalism, which is consistent with low-energy unitarity, analyticity, and crossing symmetry, seeded by an initial production amplitude. We demonstrate that the precise lineshape of the $ππ$ mass spectrum can be used to determine the relative strength and complex phase of different production mechanisms contributing to the $3π$ final state. We conduct a global fit of the $π_1$ freed-isobar data set, yielding a multi-dimensional parameterization of the $π_1\to3π$ decay amplitude at COMPASS as a function of both decay and production variables. We identify the contributions from short-range production and the Deck mechanism and extract the total $3π$ invariant mass dependence which will be important for a future extraction of the $π_1$ pole position in the $ρπ$ channel.

♻ ☆ Constraints on Complex Electroweak WIMPs from Solar Capture
Juan P. Luengas, Maxim Pospelov, Harikrishnan Ramani
One of the most convincing realizations of particle dark matter is provided by models based on electroweak multiplets. The lightest neutral state of such a multiplet can be a stable Majorana fermion or a real scalar, and its phenomenology is governed by two parameters: the dark matter mass and the mass splitting $\{m_χ,δ\}$. The sub-MeV range for $δ$ is particularly important as it allows for a large inelastic scattering cross section. In this paper, we analyze solar capture, energy loss, and annihilation of scalar and fermionic electroweak multiplet dark matter, generalizing earlier results for the Higgsino to other representations. We find that, while the case of a doublet is somewhat special, higher representations behave in a self-similar way. For the higher multiplets, IceCube results constrain the splitting to $δ\gtrsim 350$ keV for all dark matter masses up to $100$ TeV. Assuming thermal freeze-out and a Standard Halo Model velocity distribution, this rules out most models of electroweak dark matter as a possible origin of the single high-recoil event reported by the LZ collaboration. We also show that a high-velocity tail in the dark matter distribution, such as that induced by the Large Magellanic Cloud, raises the splitting preferred by the LZ event above the solar bounds for many of the multiplets.

♻ ☆ Probing Neutrino Compositeness with Invisible and Displaced Signals
Matteo Borrello, Marco Costa, Diego Redigolo, Michele Tammaro
We explore the possibility that neutrinos couple to an interacting sterile sector, providing a novel portal that generalizes the heavy neutral lepton portal to a composite setting. For a low confinement scale, high-energy neutrino beams can disintegrate into collimated sprays of hidden states, referred to as dark jets. This dynamics gives rise to two characteristic signatures in high energy neutrino beams. First, long-lived dark resonances can enhance the neutral-current to charged-current ratio. Second, shorter-lived dark states produced in neutrino neutral currents can produce single or multiple displaced vertices and even emerging jets, depending on the kinematics. These signals probe regions of parameter space beyond existing constraints from meson, electroweak, and Higgs decays, as well as from searches for displaced decays at beam dump experiments. We study these phenomena within broad classes of ultraviolet completions and identify scenarios in which high-energy neutrino beams provide leading sensitivity to neutrino compositeness. Such scenarios generically induce higher-dimensional contact interactions, which we classify and study alongside their complementary experimental signatures. Finally, we outline an experimental program spanning both the intensity and energy frontiers. Near-term neutrino facilities (DUNE, FPF) and running flavor experiments (LHCb, Belle II) can probe neutrino compositeness through neutrino disintegration into dark jets and displaced B-meson decays. Future colliders, particularly the Future Circular Collider (FCC-ee), will ultimately provide the strongest sensitivity to the compositeness scale via displaced Z decays.

♻ ☆ Chromoelectric and chromomagnetic quarkonium couplings to scalar and spin-two nucleon structure
Arkadiy I. Syamtomov
The chromoelectric and chromomagnetic polarizabilities of compact heavy quarkonium weight the scalar and spin-two structure of the nucleon differently. We derive the corresponding finite-momentum-transfer elastic response kernels, retaining the physical quarkonium velocity and nucleon spin dependence. Their correlated uncertainties are determined using lattice quark and gluon gravitational form factors. For $Υ(1S)N$ at $100\,\mathrm{MeV}$ above threshold and $Q^2=0.20\,\mathrm{GeV}^2$, the electric non-spin-flip kernel is $1.316\pm0.100_{\rm GFF}\,\mathrm{GeV}$. The electric and magnetic kernels exhibit distinct momentum-transfer and spin dependence. These kernels describe the nucleon response to the local operators. Their contributions to elastic scattering are weighted by the independent quarkonium polarizabilities.

♻ ☆ Two-loop $gg\to AA$ amplitudes near threshold and the double parton scattering singularity
Arunima Bhattacharya
The two-loop amplitudes for pseudoscalar pair production in gluon fusion, $gg\to AA$, with each pseudoscalar emitted from its own effective gluon vertex, are known in closed form, but large cancellations near threshold obscure their analytic structure. We expand the IR-finite amplitudes in the pseudoscalar velocity $β_A$ through $β_A^6$ at fixed scattering angle. All inverse powers of $β_A$ and the odd powers through $β_A^5$ cancel, and at leading power the angular dependence enters only through $\ln(2p_T/m_A)$. We identify this logarithm with the double parton scattering (DPS) singularity: with the overall constant fixed at threshold, the factorisation formula of Gaunt and Stirling reproduces the velocity dependence of its one-loop coefficient in the forward limit exactly, and a one-loop $gg\to HH$ analysis confirms the corresponding CP-even helicity sum. At two loops the equal-helicity amplitude grows as $\ln^3(2p_T/m_A)$, and the ratio of its leading two- and one-loop logarithms agrees with that in planar $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang--Mills theory, while the opposite-helicity amplitude, which has no one-loop DPS logarithm, grows as $\ln^2(2p_T/m_A)$. In the finite virtual correction, relative to the squared tree amplitude, the highest logarithm at order $α_s^2$ is $-\tfrac{7}{64}α_s^2N_c^2\ln^2(2p_T/m_A)$. For $β_A\leq0.2$ the series reproduce the unexpanded amplitudes with relative errors of at most $6.77\times10^{-5}$ at the tested points; they provide this two-loop contribution to the hard function for soft-gluon resummation of the pair invariant-mass distribution near $m_{AA}=2m_A$ and are released with code for their numerical evaluation.

♻ ☆ Magnetic field-induced enhancement and quenching of Urca emission in quark matter
William Gyory, Igor A. Shovkovy
Using first-principles field-theoretic methods, we investigate neutrino emission from strongly magnetized dense quark matter under conditions relevant to compact stars. We account for Landau-level quantization of both electron and quark states and show that it strongly modifies the kinematics of Urca processes. In particular, quark quantization restricts the available phase space in which both quark and electron energies can simultaneously lie near their respective Fermi surfaces. At moderately strong magnetic fields, before pronounced quark quantization sets in, the emission rate tends to increase on average with increasing field strength. In the regime of very strong fields, however, the increasingly restricted phase space first gives rise to Shubnikov--de Haas-type oscillations and then to resonance-like spikes near a discrete sequence of Urca-resonant magnetic field values, separated by regions of strong suppression. Finally, the emission rate becomes nearly completely quenched once $|eB| \gtrsim 6μ_{e}μ_{u}$, corresponding to approximately $B\gtrsim 1.5\times 10^{19}~\mbox{G}$ for the representative set of model parameters considered. We also find significant anisotropy in the longitudinal momentum emission near the Urca-resonant magnetic field values.

High Energy Theory [101]
☆ Scalar quasinormal modes of the exact spinning Morris--Thorne wormhole
Mark Sukaiti, Davide Batic, Denys Dutykh
We study the quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a minimally coupled massless scalar field on the exact spinning Morris-Thorne wormhole. The problem is posed on the complete two-ended geometry, whose asymptotic rest frames rotate relative to each other. After extracting the axis behaviour and the outgoing phases at both infinities, we compactify the radial coordinate and construct a quadratic eigenvalue problem by two-dimensional Chebyshev collocation. The analytic background yields exact constraints on the spectrum. At fixed azimuthal number $m$, the frequencies $\widehatω=r_0ω$ are mirror symmetric about $\operatorname{Re}\widehatω=3πjm/2$, where $r_0$ is the throat radius and $j=J/r_0^2$ is the dimensionless angular momentum. Each multipole family depends on $m$ and $j$ only through $mj$ and three angular Chebyshev polynomials represent exactly the multipoles $L=|m|,|m|+1,|m|+2$. A conserved flux confines nonthreshold real quasinormal frequencies to the superradiant window $0<ω/(mΩ_-)<1$, where $Ω_-=3πJ/r_0^3$. For the sampled sectors $m=1,2,3$ and spins up to $j=19$, every converged frequency is damped and lies outside this window. Independent integration verifies the low-lying modes, while Kerr spectra provide a separate benchmark for the two-dimensional solver. A limiting radial equation explains why the computed mode frequencies approach the upper edge of the superradiant window with frequency offsets proportional to $(mj)^{-1/2}$ at large $mj$. A complete stability assessment requires further analysis of the unresolved scalar spectrum and of perturbations of the coupled metric-matter system.
☆ Property F implies weak integrality for non-degenerate pivotal braided fusion categories
Justin Asher, Jonah Berean-Dutcher, Clay Cordova, Julio Parra-Martinez, Richard Tuddenham
We prove that every non-degenerate pivotal braided fusion category with property F is pseudo-unitary and weakly integral. In particular, every modular category with property F is weakly integral. Neither sphericality nor pseudo-unitarity is assumed. Passing to the Drinfeld centre extends the result to degenerate categories whose dimensions are positive on the intersection of the Müger centre with the adjoint subcategory; these include every braided fusion category with a pseudo-unitary Galois conjugate. Physically, the result connects the arithmetic of topological orders to the computational power of anyon braiding: non-integer squared total quantum dimension guarantees infinite braid group images, a necessary condition for universal quantum computation.

☆ Global Green-Schwarz response on quaternionic sphere bundles
Yuqi Li, Hao-Yu Sun
Local anomaly polynomials describe local variations, but a normalized Green-Schwarz phase also depends on global background data. We explain this dependence for ten-dimensional three-sphere bundles of quaternionic lines over closed spin seven-manifolds. The backgrounds retain two specified $\mathrm{Spin}(16)$ gauge bundles and an integral differential trivialization on the base, including its boundary identifications. The trivialized class is the sum of half the first Pontryagin class of the tangent bundle and the second Chern class of the quaternionic line's underlying complex bundle. For these backgrounds, the calculation combines a generally nonzero local Green-Schwarz integral with a real eta invariant evaluated by a twelve-dimensional Atiyah-Patodi-Singer filling. Together, these terms determine an integral relative characteristic number; the additive response is one third of that number, modulo integers. When the base's third and fourth rational cohomology groups vanish, the response equals eight times the Crowley-Goette invariant, without assuming that the base is simply connected. A calibration using the actual quaternionic line bundle gives additive value one third on $\mathrm{Sp}(2)$, recovering the known third-root phase. Distinct integral String data on one fixed ten-manifold give all three phase values, showing which global background information the response can detect. The physical identifications retain their prescribed fermion data, while the separate application to integral topological modular forms and vertex operator superalgebras requires compatible integral lifts. The response calculation constructs neither a microscopic realization nor an equivalence of complete theories.

We compute the cubic and $C_3\wedge X_8$ caracteristic class contributions to the trial anomaly polynomial of supersymmetric $AdS_3\times M_8$ backgrounds with $M_8=P(\mathcal O \oplus \mathcal L)\to B_6$. Including the Abelian currents descending from $C_3$, we identify the projective invariant $J$ as the denominator arising from their elimination by $c$-extremization and recover the central charge $c^{(0)}=-I_3+3I_+I_-/J$. The $X_8$ push-forward determines the pure R-symmetry, mixed R--Betti and gravitational anomalies. Evaluating it at the classical extremum gives the associated central-charge corrections, linear in the overall unshifted flux. The mixed term contributes equally to both central charges and is required in general. We evaluate these formulae for three flux-quantized backgrounds, including non-polynomial solutions. Direct projective fibre integration reproduces the mixed coefficient obtained by localization. On the wrapped-$M5$ $S^4$ bundle, the same couplings reproduce the independently known field-theory anomaly through orders $N^3$ and $N$. Their interpretation as full CFT central charges requires a unitary SCFT with a normalizable vacuum, suitable supersymmetric boundary conditions, a complete mixing sector of global currents and control of omitted anomaly sectors. A conditional Euclidean relative-equivariant interpretation is discussed separately.

☆ An efficient classical algorithm for OTOCs in chaotic quantum dynamics
Yunchao Liu, Yihui Quek, Shreya Vardhan, Tianci Zhou
Estimating out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) in individual instances of random quantum circuits has been proposed as a candidate for verifiable quantum advantage, and demonstrated to be hard for conventional classical algorithms such as tensor networks and Monte Carlo. Using insights from quantum chaos, we develop and implement a polynomial-time classical algorithm for the four-point ${\rm OTOC}^{(1)}$ and the eight-point ${\rm OTOC}^{(2)}$ in typical instances of one-dimensional (1D) quantum circuits. Our results demonstrate average-case classical tractability of estimating OTOCs in the sensitive regime where circuit-to-circuit fluctuations are large. Our algorithm organizes the OTOC into a rapidly converging series, where the leading term includes contributions from histories within permutation degrees of freedom in the replicated Hilbert space, and subleading terms arise from excursions outside this space. Although chaos is often viewed as an insurmountable barrier to classical simulation, our algorithm exploits a form of dephasing caused by chaos, which suppresses the subleading terms. We provide strong theoretical and numerical evidence to support this suppression. Further, we demonstrate that practical implementations of our algorithm estimate ${\rm OTOC}^{(1)}$ and ${\rm OTOC}^{(2)}$ in 1D circuits with high accuracy, achieving higher signal-to-noise ratio at larger circuit depths compared to recent 2D experiments by Google. Extending our algorithm to higher dimensions, and resolving the status of quantum advantage in 2D OTOCs, remain open problems.

☆ Gravitational waves and the exit from de Sitter in Inflation without an Inflaton
Daniele Bertacca, Raul Jimenez, Sabino Matarrese, Mariam Abdelaziz, Marisol Traforetti
In Inflation without an Inflaton (IWI), second-order de Sitter (dS) gravitons generate primordial curvature as the Coulomb-type potential of their gradient stress. Each pair contributes $(p/k)^2$, yielding exponential enhancement over the contributing e-folds. With exact Bunch-Davies evolution, this solution satisfies all four scalar second-order Einstein equations in pure dS. The retarded transverse-traceless solution instead has a UV kernel of order unity, $(k/p)^2$ below the scalar kernel, and a one-loop correction $Δ^2_{h,2}/Δ^2_h\simeq0.04\,Δ^2_h$. Its source acts before internal freeze-out, but oscillatory cancellations prevent tensor enhancement. We evolve the curvature through a smooth exit into radiation domination. Conserved curvature resides on the vacuum-decay hypersurface. A global depletion clock holds each scale on zero-shear time for $N_{\rm w}$ e-folds after horizon exit before local release, giving all scales equal enhancement. Energy-momentum conservation feeds the depleted vacuum energy into a non-vacuum sector, modeled as radiation. Deep in radiation domination, $Δ^2_ζ=c_wΔ_h^4e^{N_{\rm w}}/20$, with clock-dependent $c_w$, $n_s-1=-4ε$, and $n_T=-2ε$. The spectrum is adiabatic and Gaussian; super-horizon $ζ$ is conserved to better than $10^{-4}$, and changing the adiabatic exit fluid alters it by less than $0.2\%$. A direct radiation exit requires $31\lesssim N_{\rm w}\lesssim50$, or $3\times10^{-6}\lesssim r\lesssim0.036$. At interferometer frequencies, $Ω_{\rm GW}h^2\simeq2\times10^{-21}$--$3\times10^{-17}$, accessible to BBO for $r\gtrsim0.01$ and ultimate DECIGO for $r\gtrsim10^{-5}$; CMB B-mode searches probe $r\gtrsim10^{-3}$. Above $k_{\rm end}e^{-N_{\rm w}}$, the scalar spectrum steepens to $k^{-1}$, suppressing $μ$-distortions for sharp release when $N_{\rm w}\gtrsim45$.

We compute the pion quark momentum fraction in the large-$N_c$ limit using the Twisted Eguchi-Kawai (TEK) reduced model. Gauge configurations for different values of the lattice spacing are generated with the pure-gauge TEK action, while the pion correlators are computed for different quark masses with maximally twisted mass fermions. The bare matrix element corresponding to the quark momentum fraction is obtained using the Feynman-Hellmann method, and we use perturbative renormalization factors to connect to the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ scheme at $2\,\mathrm{GeV}$. A global analysis at several lattice spacings, pion masses, and values of $N_c$ yields $\langle x\rangle_q^{\overline{\mathrm{MS}}}(2\,\mathrm{GeV}) = 0.267(105)$ at the physical pion mass in the large-$N_c$ limit. This value is significantly smaller than existing $N_c=3$ determinations from phenomenology and lattice QCD, indicating that, in the large-$N_c$ limit, the pion's light-cone momentum is carried predominantly by gluons.

☆ Quality time in extra dimensions: axion quality and radion cosmology
Falguni Biswas, Yeshan Juberi, Ahmed Rakin Kamal
Higher-form symmetries can protect extra-dimensional axions, but additional symmetry breaking can still spoil the solution to the strong CP problem. Both admit Minkowski and de Sitter minima. In the sublinear regime, the relevant turning points approach the singularity. We match an exact solution of the near-singularity scaled equation to the exterior WKB solution to determine the connection matrix and spectral function. Our results thus reveal how dissipation, entanglement dynamics, and spectral properties provide complementary access to holographic geometry, establishing a unified framework for understanding the geometric information encoded in distinct boundary observables.

Symmetry defects define twisted Hilbert spaces, and the symmetry sectors are irreducible representations of the tube algebra, which acts within and between these spaces. We call this categorical RMT. For continuous symmetries, the Sugawara construction and spectral flow isolate a neutral spectrum, which can have symplectic statistics even in a bosonic theory. We compute the free energy of the model both at the free fixed point as well as the non-trivial fixed point. The model undergoes a phase transition when the temperature $T$ and angular potential attain the relation $T^2r^2\sim N (1-ω^2)$, where $ω=rΩ$ and $r$ is the radius of $S^2$, with $Tr\gg1$, at both the fixed points, with different numerical coefficients. The transition was studied earlier at zero angular potential at $Tr\sim \sqrt{N}$. The holonomy eigenvalue distribution, having support on the full circle below the transition, develops a gap above it, called the Gross-Witten-Wadia transition. The angular potential introduces an additional parameter to such a transition, tuning it, the transition can occur even at a fixed temperature. We show that for the free model transition can occur as $1-ω^2\sim 1/N$ while $Tr\sim O(1)$. For the interacting model the computation is performed at a limit $Tr\gg1$, thus we show the same at a large but fixed temperature which does not scale as $\sqrt{N}$. In the ungapped phase, the free energy exhibits a double pole near $ω^2=1$ for both the fixed points. This is possibly due to the fact that the theory projected onto the singlets is non-local and therefore need not obey the leading simple pole scaling of a local thermal effective action.

♻ ☆ Effect of ultralight dark matter on compact binary mergers

The growing catalogue of gravitational wave events enables a statistical analysis of compact binary mergers, typically quantified by the binary merger rate density. This quantity can be influenced by ambient factors, following which, in this work we have investigated the impact of dark matter environment on the merger statistics. We construct a baseline astrophysical model of eccentric and quasi-circular compact binary mergers and extend it by incorporating a model of ultra light dark matter, which affects the orbital evolution of binaries through accretion and dynamical friction. Our analysis of the merged population of binary progenitors demonstrates that, compared to the baseline model, ULDM can potentially alter the merger statistics for ambient non-zero densities, with the best agreement with GWTC-3 obtained for $ρ_0\sim10^6$ GeV/cm$^3$ and eccentricity $\sim0.5$. A comparison with the gravitational wave data from the GWTC-3 catalogue provides crucial insight into potential observational signatures of the ULDM in merger events, leading to possible constraints on the existence and density of dark matter distribution in galaxies.

♻ ☆ Explicit Symmetry Breaking in Non-Abelian Scalar Theories and One-Loop Renormalization

We investigate the one-loop renormalization of a Yang--Mills--Faddeev--Popov theory deformed by a complex scalar doublet with explicitly broken $SU(2)$ gauge symmetry. At the classical level, we map the complex doublet into a real $SO(4)$ multiplet and discuss its generalization to $SU(N)$ through $SO(2N)$. The symmetry breaking is introduced by splitting the scalar masses and quartic couplings. Using the background field method and the Schwinger--DeWitt technique, we compute the one-loop divergences and establish renormalizability at this order. We derive the beta functions, recovering the known gauge-invariant limit, and analyze the RG flow. Although the Yang--Mills coupling remains asymptotically free, the rescaled quartic couplings have no real fixed points, and the one-loop flow develops a divergence at a finite energy scale, even in the symmetric limit. The asymmetry between the rescaled scalar self-couplings increases toward the UV and decreases toward the IR, within the region of nonnegative scalar self-couplings.

♻ ☆ Spinning States and Unitarity in 3D Gravity

We revisit the proposal to cure the negative density of states in the three-dimensional gravitational path integral by adding spinning states whose spin scales with the central charge. We show that sub-extremal and extremal spinning states below the black hole threshold can cancel the known negativities, and interpret these states as bulk spinning defects. Additionally, certain overspinning states above the black hole threshold can cure these negativities while preserving the spectral gap. The overspinning states were previously interpreted as classical spinning strings; we instead identify them as overspinning BTZ geometries, which are smooth pure gravity quotients of AdS$_3$ with no fixed points. All of these spinning geometries exhibit causal pathologies in their Lorentzian continuations. Moreover, the overspinning geometries arise from mixed elliptic-hyperbolic identifications and contain a formally real chiral temperature. We also generalize the computation of scalar correlators to the extremal background and propose a quotient-motivated image expression for the overspinning geometries.

In this manuscript we consider part of the same subject using a framework in which one of the branch points of the genus two curve is fixed at infinity. This framework is a direct generalization of the popular one in the case of genus one. We address some of the issues that remained unresolved in our previous paper arXiv:2209.14633. We show that the spin structures of the simple products of fermion correlation functions with cyclic conditions depend only on the Pe-function values at the half-periods of the genus two surface, for any number of factors in the products. Similar to the genus one case, we can provide basis functions to decompose the product. Consequently, the trilinear relations found in arXiv:2211.09069 can be derived from the known set of differential equations of genus two Pe-functions by setting the variables equal to the half-periods of the non-singular and even spin structures, as is the case for genus one. Based on these considerations, we present a procedure for expressing the results of decomposed formulae in terms of the unique genus two theta function for two, three, and four point cases, and discuss a realistic approach for calculating six point function. A general formula for the expression of the results in terms of the theta function for the product of an arbitrary number of the fermion correlation functions is not yet derivable.
♻ ☆ Phonon Angular Momentum Pumping in Curved Membranes
Pablo A. Morales
Flexural vibrations dominate the low-energy spectrum of a flat crystalline membrane but do not couple to phonon Hall viscosity. We show that static curvature couples normal motion to in-plane strain, allowing an oscillatory flexural drive to generate elliptical in-plane motion and pump phonon angular momentum along the surface normal. A net angular momentum persists in randomly rippled membranes, with its magnitude and handedness controlled by the drive and ripple spectra. Transfer of the pumped angular momentum to the support produces a steady torque that reverses with the magnetic field and scales with the mean-square curvature. Using the measured bulk Hall viscosity of $α$-RuCl$_3$ to set the scale, we estimate a torque of order $10^{-23}$--$10^{-22}\,\mathrm{N\,m}$ for a few-layer membrane, within reach of demonstrated torsional sensors. The same flexural-to-shear response provides a probe of phonon Hall viscosity in atomically thin crystals.

We then develop a novel covariant Dirac bracket formalism to compute the impulse and the spin kick directly from the radial action, generalizing some conjectural results in the literature and providing ready-to-use expressions for amplitude calculations with generic spin orientations. This allows, for the first time, to find new covariant expressions for scattering observables in the probe limit up to $\mathcal{O}(G^6 s_1 s_2^4)$. Finally, we use the action-angle representation to compute the fundamental frequencies for generic bound orbits, including the intrinsic spin precession, the periastron advance and the precession of the orbital plane.

♻ ☆ Electromagnetic duality degeneracy in dynamical black hole mergers

Electromagnetic duality is a symmetry of the source-free Einstein-Maxwell equations that rotates electric and magnetic fields while leaving the stress-energy tensor invariant. We present the first fully nonlinear realization of this symmetry in dynamical strong-gravity regimes by performing numerical relativity simulations of charged black hole mergers across a continuous duality family. Starting from electrically charged binaries, we generate dyonic and magnetically charged configurations via duality rotations and evolve them within a common numerical framework. We find that all dual configurations exhibit identical spacetime dynamics, while the emitted electromagnetic radiation is related by a rotation of its polarization equal to the duality angle. Our results demonstrate a degeneracy of gravitational observables under electromagnetic duality and provide a concrete mapping between dual configurations at the level of radiation, establishing electromagnetic duality as an organizing principle for dynamical Einstein-Maxwell solutions.

♻ ☆ Landau Levels on the Surface of a Cube

We study the quantum mechanics of a charged particle confined to the surface of a cube enclosing a magnetic monopole. The magnetic field is chosen to have a constant magnitude on each face and to point along the outward normal, preserving the rotational symmetry of the cube. We formulate the continuum problem using two gauge patches on the cube surface and show that consistency of the wavefunction gives the Dirac quantization condition. Since an explicit vector potential does not remain invariant under ordinary rotations, we construct gauge-modified rotation operators and use them to classify the eigenstates. Even monopole charges are described by the irreducible representations of the cubic rotation group O, while odd monopole charges require the spinorial representations of the binary octahedral group 2O. We compute the spectrum with a gauge-covariant finite-difference discretization and find Landau-level-like manifolds whose degeneracies are split by the discrete cubic symmetry. We also study the corresponding tight-binding Hofstadter problem on the discretized cube. The resulting spectrum contains the usual magnetic subband structure together with additional gap states localized near the cube corners.

We present a background-independent renormalization framework for one-loop primordial spectra. We apply it to two observables: the scalar-induced tensor spectrum sourced by a minimally coupled spectator field, and the scalar spectrum generated by potential self-interactions. In both cases, the UV part of the loops is isolated and, using the universal WKB behavior of the internal modes, the UV poles are extracted analytically and absorbed into local counterterms without having to specify either the background evolution or the full dynamics of the field running in the loop. This yields finite model-independent expressions for the renormalized spectra amenable to numerical analysis.

♻ ☆ Discrete gravitational diagram technique and corrections to the Newtonian potential
V. M. Khatsymovsky
To develop a gravitational diagram technique that is ultraviolet finite, we start from Regge's simplicial gravity and use a bell-shaped form of the measure obtained via functional integration over connection. A "hypercubic" structure is considered (some variables are frozen), it is described by the metric $g_{λμ}$ at the sites. The measure is known in closed form if the timelike length scale is fixed at a low level. This is possible in the synchronous gauge (properly softened to remove nonphysical infrared singularities). This gauge also allows, with a refined finite-difference form of the action, to match the analytical properties of the propagator to the continuum case. The metric is parameterized to make the measure Lebesgue. The linear part of this parametrization leads to a discrete form of standard Feynman diagrams that approximates finite continuum diagrams and is finite for infinite ones; the nonlinear part gives new vertices and diagrams. The maximum of the measure is at the edge length scale $b = b_{\rm s} \sim η^{1/2}$, where $η$ defines the free factor like $(- \det \|g_{λμ}\|)^{η/2}$ in the measure and should be a large parameter to ensure true action upon integration over connection. For general perturbative expansion (including both that for the measure and the S matrix) to be free of increasing powers of $η$, its initial point must be at $b$ sufficiently close to $b_{\rm s}$; this appears to be a dynamic mechanism for establishing $b$ as an optimal initial point of the perturbative expansion. This technique is applied to Newton's potential. Some of new diagrams, including potentially large ones, are mutually cancelled. The S matrix expansion is analyzed to consist of standard diagrams. These diagrams form series with a small parameter $η^{-1}$; one-loop diagrams calculated in the literature represent the leading order.

♻ ☆ Gravitational Waves from Multiple Cosmic Superstrings and the Overshoot Problem
Luca Brunelli, Michele Cicoli, Muhammad Hassan, Seyed Ehsan Qoreishi, Francisco Gil Pedro
Post inflationary string cosmology can feature an initial population of multiple species of cosmic superstrings whose tension is controlled by a modulus rolling over a steep potential toward a late-time minimum. We perform a full analysis of the associated dynamical system, finding that overshooting the minimum is prevented by the friction of a radiation background of gravitational waves produced from the early decay of effective strings arising from NS5- and D3-branes wrapped around internal cycles. On the other hand, fundamental strings survive longer and decay when the modulus is oscillating around the minimum and they have about $1/3$ of the total energy density. The spectrum of gravitational waves generated by the decays of these multiple cosmic superstrings, even if diluted by a late epoch of modulus domination, can still result in a high-frequency, multi-peaked signal, offering an observational signature of generic features of string theory.

♻ ☆ A Common Type II Origin of Galilean and Carroll Superstrings
Mehmet Ozkan, Utku Zorba
We show that the relativistic Type-II superalgebras, once the fundamental-string winding charge is retained alongside the momentum, admit a single non-Lorentzian contraction with two invariant translation ideals, whose complementary quotients yield Galilean and magnetic-Carroll superalgebras. The complementary vector charge required for this structure is thus intrinsic to string theory. The IIA realization is particle-like and the IIB realization string-like, a distinction fixed by chirality, and spacelike T-duality relates the two while preserving each non-Lorentzian structure. The same contraction is finite on the doubled Green--Schwarz action, including all fermion terms and local kappa symmetry, where the two supersymmetries appear as the two polarizations of a single worldsheet theory. These results unify two distinct non-Lorentzian corners of string theory within a common Type-II origin and open a route toward a broader web of non-Lorentzian dualities and possible holographic generalizations.

♻ ☆ The running of Weyl gauged gravity: asymptotic freedom, its obstruction, and a way out
Diego Buccio, Fabrizio Chicconi, Luca Parente, Omar Zanusso
We compute the one-loop beta functions of quadratic gravity in Weyl conformal geometry, the gauge theory of diffeomorphisms and dilatations with a dynamical Weyl gauge boson. The divergences are extracted diagrammatically in the background field method, with a gauge fixing procedure adapted to the semidirect product structure of the gauge group. The Weyl-tensor coupling and the Weyl gauge coupling are asymptotically free, and the running of the latter is special, being independent of the other couplings and of any two-derivative matter content. The obstruction to an ultraviolet completion comes from the square of a Weyl-covariant curvature scalar, denoted $\widehat{R}{}^2$: the flow of the corresponding coupling has no fixed point in the physically interesting region and becomes trivial, the only real fixed points require a decoupled Weyl boson and a tachyonic scalar mode. This also holds when including the Standard Model with any nonminimal Higgs coupling and, more generally, for any matter with two-derivative kinetic terms. Weyl-invariant four-derivative scalars with a sufficiently large coupling to $\widehat{R}{}^2$ can remove the obstruction, producing a fixed point in the physical region that is ultraviolet attractive in all directions and has a nonvanishing Weyl gauge coupling.

♻ ☆ Particle dynamics in rotating charged Bumblebee black holes: An analytical correspondence with Kerr-Newman

In this paper, we establish an analytical correspondence between the equatorial dynamics of spinless and spinning test particles in a slowly rotating charged Einstein--Bumblebee black hole spacetime and those in an effective Kerr--Newman spacetime. For spinning particles, the correspondence is established within the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon framework under appropriate parameter matching. We show that corresponding circular orbits have identical radii and coordinate angular velocities, while their radial dynamics and local instability rates exhibit a Lorentz-violation-dependent scaling. Nevertheless, the correspondence does not imply complete dynamical equivalence, as orbital trajectories and radial perturbation growth over an azimuthal period generally differ. These results delineate the scope and limitations of the effective Kerr--Newman correspondence by distinguishing the dynamical properties preserved under parameter matching from those modified by the Lorentz-violating radial deformation.

♻ ☆ Collective excitations in quantum gravity condensates
Andrea Calcinari, Adrià Delhom, Daniele Oriti
A central open problem in quantum gravity is to understand how continuum spacetime emerges from quantum-geometric degrees of freedom in a background-independent setting. A many-body perspective suggests that spacetime emerges as a hydrodynamic phase of many atoms of quantum geometry. This idea underlies several approaches to quantum gravity, and it has been explicitly realised in the group field theory formalism. However, quantum fluctuations beyond the mean-field regime remain largely unexplored. We fill this gap by importing Bogolyubov theory to quantum gravity condensates, showing that leading beyond-mean-field effects manifest as collective excitations, in direct analogy with phonons in laboratory Bose-Einstein condensates. We implement the construction in a tractable group field theory model, where condensates of quantum-geometric atoms reproduce nonsingular expanding cosmologies, and derive the leading beyond-mean-field corrections to the emergent Friedmann dynamics. These results identify a new class of quantum-gravity excitations and establish a controlled bridge between microscopic quantum-gravitational dynamics, many-body collective phenomena, and signatures of spacetime emergence.

♻ ☆ Exploring the near-kernel sector of quantum reduced loop gravity
Ilkka Mäkinen, Hanno Sahlmann, Waleed Sherif
We study the near-kernel sector of the Hamiltonian constraint operator in the one-vertex model of quantum reduced loop gravity using exact diagonalisation methods and variational Monte Carlo methods with neural quantum states. The analysis is based on the symmetric Hamiltonian containing both Euclidean and Lorentzian contributions, and on the variational minimization of the positive quadratic operator $\hat{Q}=\hat{C}^2$, where $\hat{C}$ is the symmetric Hamilton constraint, in truncated Hilbert spaces with spin cutoff up to $j_\text{max}=1001$. In the cases where exact diagonalization is possible, the eigenspace of lowest eigenvalue is one- or two-dimensional, and the eigenvalue, as well as the structure of the eigenstates depends on the cutoff. These ground states are entangled across the three edges. The variational method does not find the lowest eigenspace, but near kernel states, i.e., states with components in a number of low lying eigenspaces. For low cutoffs, they also do not factorize across the three edge degrees of freedom. At larger cutoffs, it increasingly finds near kernel states that factorize over the edges, matched with near-unit fidelity by reduced Thiemann coherent states. We discuss some indication that these states are the optimal near-kernel states if factorization is assumed.

We revisit the Schwarzschild singularity in a semiclassical setting where the background geometry is classical and quantum effects enter through Bohmian (quantal) trajectories associated with a Klein-Gordon wave function. Using the Madelung-Bohm decomposition of the Klein-Gordon wavefunction, we show that the quantum-modified motion is equivalent to geodesic motion in an effective metric conformally related to Schwarzschild, with a conformal factor fixed by the wavefunction amplitude. Solving the wavefunction equation near $r\to 0$ determines this factor and yields finite curvature invariants, in suitable coordinates the interior extends smoothly and the effective spacetime is geodesically complete. Our result suggests that quantum probes on a prescribed classical background can experience an operationally regular effective geometry, even though the underlying Schwarzschild spacetime itself remains classically singular.

We study the Hall viscosity of the quark gluon plasma (QGP) created in non-central heavy-ion collisions. In the presence of a strong magnetic field or vorticity, rotational symmetry is broken from $O(3)$ to $O(2)$, allowing for two independent Hall viscosities associated with shear deformations transverse and parallel to the symmetry-breaking direction. We find the corresponding constitutive relations by extending the kinetic-theory mechanism to three spatial dimensions and provide parametric estimates of the Hall viscosities under realistic QGP conditions. Both kinetic-theory and holographic estimates indicate that Hall viscosities are comparable in magnitude to the shear viscosity at zero magnetic field. ♻ ☆ Rapid Graviton Thermalization through a Scalar--Gauss--Bonnet Coupling

We show that gravitons can thermalize much faster than the universe expands in an effective scalar-mediated model. A thermal fermion bath maintains a massive scalar close to equilibrium, while scalar decay and inverse decay, $φ\rightleftarrows g+g$, drive the graviton distribution toward a Bose--Einstein distribution with zero chemical potential. We establish this equilibrium state and calculate how it is reached from an initially empty graviton sector. For a scalar mass of $1\,{\rm TeV}$, an interaction scale $Λ_{\rm int}=m_φ/0.03$, and a Yukawa coupling $y=0.03$, the graviton occupations approach their equilibrium values to within $0.1\%$ over $0.1\leq p/T\leq5$ after approximately $0.024$ initial Hubble times, including cosmic expansion and energy transfer from the bath. This interval contains the thermal energy-spectrum peak. The scalar remains close to equilibrium, its vacuum decay widths are narrow, and the graviton interaction is perturbative over the reaction domain. Assuming the effective theory applies on this domain, our results demonstrate that gravitons can reach near-thermal equilibrium under these conditions. We also derive the present-day thermal spectrum for a specified decoupling and entropy history.

We study the boundary preparation of strong Mpemba states in a probe Abelian Higgs model on a fixed AdS black brane. For a representative protocol, the slow amplitude is reduced by a factor of about 600 relative to linear cancellation. This extends the fast relaxation window without changing the final quasinormal mode spectrum. Further nonlinear tuning suppresses the estimated residual amplitude to the level of numerical resolution. The prepared states can overtake a weakly driven reference despite having a larger excess free energy at source removal. Three pulses also suppress a second slow channel over the resolved time window and reveal interference between faster modes. Starting from a common initial state, controls with zero net charge transfer reach a given relaxation threshold sooner than passive relaxation, even when the full control duration is included.

We explicitly compute the axial anomaly in dense matter and show that it takes the same form as in vacuum, even in the massless limit. This result follows from a subtle cancellation in the anomalous Ward identity between the medium-induced contributions to the divergence of the axial current and to the pseudoscalar density. We then revisit the chiral magnetic effect in a fermionic medium coupled to an axial chemical potential in an external magnetic field. We show that, in the clean limit, the medium supports a persistent, conserved anomalous current carried by fermions. The current is determined by the axial chemical potential and suppressed by the Fermi velocity, in agreement with anomalous axial-current correlation functions. Finally, we discuss applications to axion physics, where axion dark matter acts as an effective axial chemical potential, and estimate how helicity relaxation by impurity scattering limits the induced current in realistic conductors.

For $f(Q)$ gravity coupled with scalar, we obtain ACT inflation for large classes of $f(Q)$ via the choice of the scalar potentials. The entropic cosmology based on generalised entropy, which includes most of the known entropies like Tsallis, Rényi, Barrow, etc as a particular case, is investigated. The corresponding FRW equations, depending on the parameters of generalised entropy, are presented. Using the correspondence between the generalised entropy and $f(Q)$ gravity, we obtain generalised entropic inflation, which is consistent with the ACT-DR6. At the next step, the entropic gravity coupled with scalar is considered. It is demonstrated how one can obtain ACT-DR6-consistent inflation for such a theory based on any generalised entropy considered in this paper via the choice of scalar potentials. These findings may point towards the correct unifying entropy of the early universe.

♻ ☆ On Generalized Statistics and Stability in $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-Graded Supersymmetric Yang-Mills Theory
Ren Ito, Akio Nago, Shou Tanigawa
In the standard formulation of relativistic quantum field theory, a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded structure is assumed to realize locality and the boson-fermion dichotomy. While $\mathbb{Z}_2^n$-graded extensions are known to be allowed at the level of symmetry, their realization in interacting quantum field theories remains unclear. In this paper, we construct a classical minimal $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory. We derive the invariant action and show that all kinetic terms have the correct sign, indicating the absence of classical ghost-like instabilities. Moreover, the positivity of the Hamiltonian follows from the $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded supersymmetry algebra. As a result, we show that $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded generalized statistics can be realized at the classical level in a stable interacting supersymmetric gauge theory.

We discuss the finite-$N$ Hilbert space of bilocal operators that underlies bilocal holography of vector models, beyond the sector built on the Fock vacuum. If the microscopic oscillator Fock space carries a multiplicity-free dual action of a compact color group $G$ and a bilocal algebra, Howe duality implies that projection to the derived subgroup $[G,G]$ selects precisely the characters of the abelianization $G^{\rm ab}=G/[G,G]$ that occur in the Fock space. Thus $O(N)/SO(N)=\mathbb Z_2$ gives two sectors, $U(N)/SU(N)=U(1)$ gives integer determinant-charge sectors, while $Sp(N)$ is perfect and gives no additional sector; Bose/Fermi statistics and the number of modes determine which sectors are actually realized. Around each new background we solve the constraints with auxiliary oscillators, which form a Fermi sea for bosonic matter. In the free vector model on $\mathbb R\times S^2$ the lowest states in the new sectors are baryonic primaries; we determine their energies, degeneracies and spin content exactly at finite $N$, together with their lowest energy at fixed angular momentum.

Transporting the states, kernels and inverse chains together gives a finite Ward identity and coefficientwise reconstruction for that chosen family. The condensate, expected to break the symmetries of hyperbolic space, instead preserves them outside a layer at the entangling surface, whose width diverges at $n_*$ with Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless scaling. The universal term of the Rényi entropy therefore jumps at $n_*$ to that of the symmetry-breaking defect. We demonstrate this mechanism in the probe Abelian Higgs model in AdS$_5$ at the Bogomolny point, with closed-form saddles and defect data, and numerical flows. For a ball we prove that a positive source-free flow exists exactly when $n>n_*$ and the radius is large enough, and that it ends at the symmetry-breaking defect as the radius grows.

We present theoretical and experimental evidence to show that this method is highly effective and efficient at the task. Our method obtains better or similar accuracy scores to commonly used methods while having a major computational speedup.

In Weyl materials, density-wave gaps have been linked to axion-like magnetoelectric response, placing the charge-density-wave phase within a dynamical-field description of the effective action. These developments have led to the term "topological charge density wave," but the phrase describes several physically distinct phenomena. We distinguish three meanings: (i) topology of the order parameter and its defects, (ii) topology of the charge-density-wave-reconstructed electronic structure and its boundary modes, and (iii) axion-like electromagnetic response generated by density-wave order. The experimental and theoretical support for these three meanings differs substantially. This Perspective traces the development of these ideas, clarifies the evidence behind each class, identifies unresolved questions and points of debate, and outlines experimental criteria for establishing topology in charge-density-wave states.

More broadly, these results demonstrate that conventional force metrics can provide an incomplete assessment of downstream performance and highlights the importance of evaluating scientific machine-learning models within computational workflows.

♻ ☆ Spherical Balls Settling Through a Quiescent Cement Paste Measured by X-ray Tomography: Influence of the Paste Thixotropy
Subhransu Dhar, Eduardo Machado-Charry, Robert Schennach, Teresa Liberto, Agathe Robisson
The settling of spherical balls in quiescent cement pastes of increasing age is studied. Metallic spheres with radii of 2, 2.5 and 3mm are dropped into the paste and allowed to settle, while their position is tracked using X-ray tomography. The instantaneous velocity of the spheres, calculated from their movement, is observed to be quasi-constant during their fall, and an average is estimated. The results show that the average velocity of the balls decreases logarithmically with paste age until ball stoppage, for all three ball sizes. In parallel, the rheological properties of the cement paste are measured using a rheometer with a vane geometry. The evolution of the paste static yield stress over time is evaluated, and proves to be a reliable predictor for ball stoppage. Finally, thixotropic models of increasing complexity are evaluated. These models consider four forms of structural growth and breakdown parameters, and their ability to capture the ball settling velocity as a function of paste age is compared. This emphasizes the importance of considering paste breakdown in relation to shearing of the paste when the ball passes through it.
♻ ☆ Ta-based S-I-S junctions for integrated superconducting electronics
Trent Borman, Cameron Bullock, Cole Chason, Bradley Christensen, Jonathan Cochran, Emad Din, Evan Donohue, Jason Flagg, A. L. Graninger, Eric Jones, Robert Klaes, Shawn Keebaugh, Erin Kennedy, John Kula, Jason Lapano, Melissa Loving, Christopher Pasco, Devika Pathak, Tam Pham, Timothy Pillsbury, Robert Pownall, Paige Quarterman, Jacob Ruf, Jade Simmons, Nathan Siwak, Joel Strand, Yong Mo Yang
In this work, we have presented S-I-S Josephson junctions with $\rmα$-Ta electrodes and a ${\rm TaO}_x$ barrier. We grew base and top $α$-Ta electrodes using seed layer engineering, showing both Nb and ${\rm TaN}_x$ are viable seed layer choices, and particularly emphasize that at room temperature a re-seed layer is required to nucleate $\rmα$-Ta for the top electrode. However, we note that the choice of seed layer can have subtle implications on the electrical tunneling behavior of the junctions. We used room-temperature probing of variable junction areas, combined with Ambegaokar-Baratoff physics, to characterize the wafer scale critical current densities. For 0.4 $μ$m$^2$ junctions, we found junction spreads as low as 2.0% across the 20 x 20 mm chip relevant for device performance. The entire process was carried out using standard industry foundry processing using 150 mm wafer tooling, which is an important step towards proving that Ta-based junctions can be implemented at scale. We have successfully fabricated and tested junctions with $\rmα$-Ta electrodes and a ${\rm TaO}_x$ insulating tunnel barrier, demonstrating that this is a material platform which merits further investigation and studies for potential application in classical and quantum superconducting technologies.

♻ ☆ Anharmonic lattice dynamics and superconductivity in strained bulk and surface niobium

Using first-principles calculations, we investigate how homogeneous strain and crystallographic surface orientation modify the vibrational and superconducting properties of niobium. For bulk Nb, tensile strain strongly softens the phonon spectrum and enhances the electron--phonon coupling, increasing the superconducting transition temperature from 9.5 K at equilibrium to 14.5 K at $\sim\!6\%$ lattice expansion. For the low-index Nb(001), Nb(110), and Nb(111) surfaces, harmonic phonon calculations exhibit imaginary modes, showing that anharmonic lattice effects are essential. To treat these effects efficiently, we train Nb-specific machine-learning interatomic potentials on bulk and slab first-principles configurations and use them to accelerate stochastic self-consistent harmonic approximation calculations, thereby obtaining anharmonically renormalized phonon modes that are combined with density-functional perturbation theory electron--phonon matrix elements to construct the Eliashberg spectral function. Among the clean free-standing slabs considered here, Nb(001) exhibits the strongest electron--phonon coupling and the highest calculated transition temperature of 10.0 K, while Nb(110) and Nb(111) show progressively reduced pairing strength. Finally, by analyzing the Eliashberg spectral function and the functional derivative $δT_\text{c}/δα^2F(ω)$, we identify the phonon energy ranges most effective for superconducting pairing. Our results show that strain, surface termination, and anharmonic phonon renormalization provide complementary and interrelated microscopic routes for tuning superconductivity in Nb.

The ruby lattice has been the subject of much interest recently due to its realization in Rydberg atom arrays, where its rich variety of frustrated interactions gives rise to topologically ordered quantum spin liquids. Similarly, numerical studies of ruby-lattice spin models, with both isotropic and anisotropic interactions, have provided evidence of gapped and gapless spin-liquid ground states with different low-energy gauge structures. Motivated by these findings, we perform a projective symmetry group (PSG) classification of U(1) and $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ fermionic spinon mean-field theories$\unicode{x2014}$respecting space-group and time-reversal symmetries$\unicode{x2014}$for $S=1/2$ spins. We obtain a total of 50 U(1) and 64 $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ PSGs, and upon restricting their realization via mean-field $\textit{Ansätze}$ with up to second-nearest-neighbor singlet amplitudes (relevant to the models studied here), only 8 U(1) and 18 $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ distinct states are obtained. We present the singlet fields for all $\textit{Ansätze}$ up to third-nearest-neighboring bonds and discuss their spinon dispersions as well as their dynamical spin structure factors. Building on this information, we also obtain the phase diagram of the Heisenberg model in the presence of first- ($J_{1}$), second- ($J_{1}'$), and third- ($J_{2}$) neighbor antiferromagnetic couplings within a self-consistent mean-field approximation.

♻ ☆ Challenges in Non-Polymeric Crystal Structure Prediction: Why a Geometric, Permutation-Invariant Loss is Needed
Emmanuel Jehanno, Romain Menegaux, Julien Mairal, Sergei Grudinin
Crystalline structure prediction is an essential prerequisite for designing materials with targeted properties. Yet, it is still an open challenge in materials design and drug discovery. Despite recent advances in computational materials science, accurately predicting three-dimensional non-polymeric crystal structures remains elusive. In this work, we focus on the molecular assembly problem, where a set~$\mathcal{S}$ of identical rigid molecules is packed to form a crystalline structure. Such a simplified formulation provides a useful approximation to the actual problem. However, while recent state-of-the-art methods have increasingly adopted sophisticated techniques, the underlying learning objective remains ill-posed. We propose a better formulation that introduces a loss function capturing key geometric molecular properties while ensuring permutation invariance over $\mathcal{S}$. Remarkably, we demonstrate that within this framework, a simple regression model already outperforms prior approaches, including flow matching techniques, on the COD-Cluster17 benchmark, a curated non-polymeric subset of the Crystallography Open Database (COD). Our code is available at https://github.com/inria-thoth/SinkFast.
♻ ☆ Light in Slices: How to Enable Precise Laser Processing?
Stefan Nolte, Jörn Bonse, Nadezhda M. Bulgakova
Ultrashort (femtosecond, fs) laser pulses have fascinating properties as they allow to confine optical energy on extreme scales in space and time. Such fs-laser pulsed beams can be seen as spatially thin slices of intense light that are radially and axially constrained to the micrometer scale, while simultaneously propagating at the extremely high speed of light. Their high peak intensities and their short time lapse makes such laser pulses unique tools for materials processing, as their duration is shorter than the time required to transfer absorbed optical energy, via electron-phonon coupling, from the electronic system of the solid to its lattice. Hence, the laser pulse energy remains localized during the interaction and does not spread via diffusion into the area surrounding the irradiated region. As one consequence, the fs-laser thus offers increased precision for material modification or ablation accompanied by a reduced heat-affected zone of only a few hundred nanometers. On the other hand, the high laser peak intensities can enable nonlinear material interactions that are rendering unique material excitation and relaxation pathways possible. In this chapter, we briefly review the reasons for the enormous success of ultrashort pulse lasers in materials processing - both for the processing of the surface or in the bulk of solids. We identify the underlying fundamental processes that can limit the precision or the up-scaling of the laser processing towards large volumes, areas, or processing rates. Strategies to overcome such limitations will be outlined and questions on the ultimate limits of laser material processing will be answered.

♻ ☆ An Extensible Agentic Framework for Expert-Level Automation of Atomistic Simulations
Yutack Park, Yeonwoo Chung, Jinmu You, Jisu Kim, Suyeon Ju, Seungwu Han
Traditionally, atomistic simulation has been constrained by the computational scaling limits of ab initio methods and the parameterization overhead of empirical force fields. The recent emergence of universal machine learning interatomic potentials has significantly mitigated these bottlenecks, offering near-quantum accuracy and generalizability across diverse chemical spaces at a fraction of the computational cost. However, this shift has relocated the bottleneck to the human dimension: time-consuming mechanical processes, such as input preparation and data analysis, now dominate the research lifecycle. We introduce Paimon, a Platform for Agentic Integration in Materials Optimization and Nanoscale-simulations. Through hundreds of trials on an expert-level liquid electrolyte simulation, we show that Paimon substantially improves the reliability of agentic workflows by suppressing silent errors: plausible yet physically incorrect results. Paimon accommodates a new capability without modifying the agents already present, which we demonstrate by integrating an externally developed scientific agent. As an agent harness for atomistic simulations, Paimon affords researchers a continuous, science-centric workflow throughout the entire simulation lifecycle.

♻ ☆ QT-Net: Rethinking Evaluation of AI Models in Atomic Chemical Space

In this work, we propose a held-out evaluation protocol that clusters atomic environments by SOAP descriptors and computes metrics accounting only for cluster labels unseen during training. Following this procedure, we use 5$\times$5 cross-validation and Tukey's HSD to run a statistically rigorous comparison of E(3)-equivariant against non-equivariant, rotationally augmented models for predicting electron populations and multipoles of H, C, N, and O atoms. Building on our results, we introduce the Quantum Topological Neural Network (QT-Net), a rotationally augmented, non-equivariant graph neural network. We show that QT-Net can be used to infer properties of atoms in molecules from QM9 outside our training set, and that the atomic environments seen during training strongly affect the performance of molecular property prediction tasks. To further validate the framework, molecular dipole moments computed from QT-Net's per-atom outputs recover the ground-truth values reported in QM9. We release all code and data, including a JAX implementation of QT-Net.
♻ ☆ Advances in electrical contacts to single crystals of emerging materials for transport measurements
Huandong Chen, Abhay N. Pasupathy, Jayakanth Ravichandran
Transport measurements that probe electrical resistivity of a material under varying external stimuli, such as temperature, magnetic field, optical illumination, and gate voltage, are among the most important experimental techniques in condensed matter physics. These measurements provide critical insights into the fundamental electronic properties of materials. In recent years, they have facilitated the discovery and exploration of intriguing physical phenomena (e.g., superconductivity and quantum oscillations) and unique device functionalities (e.g., photoresponse and electrostatic gating effects) in various emerging materials, particularly in the form of single crystals. However, unlike large-scale wafers or thin films, newly synthesized single crystals often pose substantial challenges in establishing reliable electrical contacts due to their irregular geometries, limited dimensions, inherent structural characteristics, and potential susceptibility to degradation. In this review, we highlight recent technological advancements in the fabrication of high-quality, lithographically defined multi-terminal electrodes on both exfoliable and non-exfoliable single crystals for transport measurements. Our work provides a practical guide for researchers seeking to select appropriate contact-fabrication strategies tailored to unique characteristics of emerging crystals.
♻ ☆ Anatomy of fast current-induced skyrmion motion in synthetic antiferromagnets
W. C. Chen, H. X. Yang, X. F. Zhang
The high mobility of current-driven skyrmions in synthetic antiferromagnets (SAFs) is widely explained by the macroscopic suppression of the skyrmion Hall effect through gyrotropic force compensation. This established view, however, overlooks a concurrent and significant reduction in the Gilbert damping parameter α, a key factor in the Thiele equation governing skyrmion velocity. Here, we show that this damping attenuation originates from a reconfigured magnon-electron scattering landscape. Using a microscopic s-d model, we demonstrate that the strong antiferromagnetic interlayer Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) exchange coupling in SAFs increases the magnonic gap of skyrmion collective modes, thereby suppressing the thermal magnon population and, consequently, the magnon-electron scattering rate that dominates damping in metallic ferromagnets. Our work establishes a dual-mechanism framework to fully explain the superior kinetics of SAF skyrmions: the macroscopic topological effect rectifies the motion direction, while the microscopic dissipation mechanism reduces the drag. This synergy enables high-speed and efficient motion, providing a fundamental elucidation of the enhanced mobility reported in recent studies such as the work by Pham et al. [Science 384, 307-312 (2024)].

♻ ☆ Towards Multiscale Molecular Representation Learning through Geometry-Based Fragmentation for Polymer Property Prediction
Makoto Takamoto, Chaitanya Sampara, Viktor Zaverkin, Daniel Oñoro-Rubio, Mathias Niepert
It is well established that molecular substructures can contribute unequally to chemical and physical properties, with specific motifs or side chains often playing dominant roles. Fragment-based representations have therefore emerged as an effective strategy for incorporating chemically meaningful inductive biases, as exemplified by molecular fingerprints and fragment-based attention mechanisms. However, many existing fragmentation-based machine learning methods rely on predefined chemical rules, which may yield suboptimal fragmentation for previously unseen or chemically unfamiliar structures and often overlook the importance of multiscale molecular representations. To address these limitations, we formulate molecular fragmentation as a radius-constrained optimization problem inspired by the k-center formulation, where the number of clusters is not fixed a priori but emerges from the specified radius, and propose a geometry-based fragmentation method that partitions arbitrary molecular or material structures using largely geometric information, without relying on predefined chemical fragmentation rules. The method provides flexible control over fragment size, enabling the construction of multiscale fragment representations for scale-adaptive modeling. Building on this framework, we develop a geometric fragment-based attention mechanism that integrates multiscale structural information and incorporate it into a multimodal machine learning model combining p-SMILES representations with three-dimensional (3D) conformational information. Experiments on a benchmark polymer dataset show that incorporating 3D conformational information improves prediction accuracy for several properties over models based exclusively on p-SMILES representations. Explainable artificial intelligence analyses further provide insights into the physical relevance of the learned representations.

♻ ☆ Universal Scaling and Geometric Correction of High-Frequency Mass Transfer in Porous Electrodes
Md Abdul Hamid, Kyle C. Smith
Classical film theory predicts a finite diffusion-limited current at porous electrodes. Transient operation can nevertheless produce peak interfacial fluxes above this steady limit, although the time-averaged flux remains bounded. Here, we use a frequency-domain volume-averaging framework to study this transient response in porous media. In the perfectly reactive limit, the spectral Sherwood number approaches $\Shnd\sim\sqrt{\iu\wstar}$ at high frequency, with magnitude proportional to $ω^{1/2}$, phase $π/4$, and a universal leading prefactor. A boundary-layer analysis shows that this response follows from local transient diffusion and is independent of the global pore geometry. Numerical results for parallel plates, circular tubes, and twelve porous microstructures confirm the scaling across variations in particle shape, symmetry, porosity, array arrangement, flow orientation, and flow strength. We also derive the first geometry-dependent correction, which depends on interfacial area, surface curvature, and sharp edges, and verify it without fitted parameters. Comparisons with published impedance measurements for a carbon-felt fiber and a vanadium flow-battery electrode are consistent with the predicted transport response. Finally, we derive bounds on pulse duration and identify operating windows for representative redox couples. These results establish a temporal route to enhanced peak transport in porous electrodes without requiring surface charge, confinement, or electrokinetic instability.
♻ ☆ Linker Functionalization and pH Tuning Enhance Solar-Driven Catalytic CO$_2$ Reduction in MOF-5

The wide band gap of metal-organic framework (MOF) 5 constrains its use in photocatalytic carbon dioxide (CO$_2$) reduction despite its high porosity and favorable mass-transport properties. Adopting a state-of-the-art first-principles approach, we systematically investigate the effects of volumetric strain, metal-node substitution, linker functionalization, and pH control as knobs to improve the CO$_2$ photocatalytic ability of MOF-5. Strain and metal-node substitution negligibly affect the gap, whereas linker functionalization narrows it into the visible range via in-gap states while preserving reduction-side alignment at pH = 0. The resulting reduction energetics are strongly sensitive to both linker functionalization and pH. Halogenated and hydroxylated frameworks provide access primarily to HCOOH, CO, and HCHO under alkaline conditions, principally with the Mg and Zn nodes, whereas COOH functionalization offers the broadest thermodynamic accessibility across the full CO$_2$ reduction sequence. NH$_2$ retains thermodynamic feasibility for all target reduction pathways but with larger overpotentials, while NO$_2$ generally yields unfavorable reduction energetics. Crucially, within the COOH series, the choice of the metal node tunes the fundamental gap by over 1 eV with only minor changes in the reduction overpotentials, placing Sr- and Ba-based architectures as the most favorable ones for broad product selectivity with visible-light excitation. Linker functionalization substantially reduces the spatial overlap of the frontier states, promoting photoinduced charge separation. Taken together, these results establish linker functionalization and solution pH as complementary design levers for independently tuning light absorption and CO$_2$-reduction energetics in MOF-5, establishing a rational and viable route for designing efficient MOF-based photocatalysts.

Kohei Ishii, Hisazumi Akai, Tetsuya Fukushima, Hikari Shinya, Hyuga Hosoi, Noritsugu Sakuma, Koji Inui
Discovering solid-state materials with target properties remains a central challenge in computational materials science. Here we develop a first-principles inverse-design framework that requires no training data. Any differentiable quantity computable within KKR-CPA can serve as an optimization objective. We demonstrate this generality in permanent-magnet and half-metal design, identifying candidates such as (Nd$_{0.983}$Pr$_{0.017}$)(Co$_{0.72}$Fe$_{0.28}$)$_2$Fe$_3$ and FeMn(As$_{0.83}$P$_{0.17}$), respectively. We also synthesized materials with five SmCo$_5$-based compositions selected during optimization for higher magnetization. Their measured magnetization agreed closely with calculated values. The damping of the optical plasmons at low energy, however, is strongly influenced by the reduced scattering rates described in the marginal Fermi liquid model for "strange-metal" behavior. In addition, the same model describes the linear-in-energy damping of acoustic plasmons. In several material classes, charge-density-wave order reshapes electronic bands, boundary states, defect structures, and electromagnetic responses in ways that invite a topological interpretation. Real-space imaging has shown that incommensurate order can form networks of phase defects rather than uniform modulations. Boundary-resolved spectroscopy has revealed in-gap modes whose existence and spatial structure track the charge-density-wave order, although such observations remain confined to a single material family. In Weyl materials, density-wave gaps have been linked to axion-like magnetoelectric response, placing the charge-density-wave phase within a dynamical-field description of the effective action. In kagome metals, charge order is intertwined with Berry curvature, unconventional symmetry breaking, and superconductivity. These developments have led to the term "topological charge density wave," but the phrase describes several physically distinct phenomena. We distinguish three meanings: (i) topology of the order parameter and its defects, (ii) topology of the charge-density-wave-reconstructed electronic structure and its boundary modes, and (iii) axion-like electromagnetic response generated by density-wave order. The experimental and theoretical support for these three meanings differs substantially. This Perspective traces the development of these ideas, clarifies the evidence behind each class, identifies unresolved questions and points of debate, and outlines experimental criteria for establishing topology in charge-density-wave states.

We propose its analogue for local quantum systems on a circle with ordinary or non-invertible symmetries. Symmetry defects define twisted Hilbert spaces, and the symmetry sectors are irreducible representations of the tube algebra, which acts within and between these spaces. Under our proposal, the symmetry fixes exact degeneracies and identifications among sectors, and ordinary RMT describes the rest, with unrelated blocks treated as statistically independent. We call this categorical RMT. For a non-invertible symmetry it goes beyond ordinary RMT, since Hilbert spaces with different twists can share a sector, and so part of their spectrum, though no invertible symmetry relates them. For continuous symmetries, the Sugawara construction and spectral flow isolate a neutral spectrum, which can have symplectic statistics even in a bosonic theory.
